question: What is the main job of vitamin D made in the skin?

options.D: Promoting calcium absorption in the gut

explanation: Vitamin D made in the skin changes into an active form that helps the intestines absorb calcium from the food you eat. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h1)

question: How does the skin help lower a high body temperature?

options.A: Constricting blood vessels to trap heat internally
options.B: Dilating dermal blood vessels and producing sweat
options.C: Increasing subcutaneous fat deposition for insulation
options.D: Shedding outer epidermal cells to release body heat

explanation: Blood vessels widen to bring warm blood close to the skin surface to release heat, while sweat evaporation cools the body down. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h1)

question: Which skin cell type is mainly responsible for producing protective skin color?
explanation: Melanocytes make melanin, the pigment that absorbs ultraviolet light to protect deep skin cells from damage. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h2)

question: How does the outer layer of the skin (epidermis) get its nutrients?

options.A: Absorption of moisture from the external air
options.B: Diffusion from blood vessels in the dermis
options.C: Direct capillary loops reaching the outer surface
options.D: Active transport via lymphatic vessel networks

explanation: The epidermis does not have its own blood supply, so nutrients soak upward from the blood vessels in the layer beneath it. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h2)

question: Where on the body is the clear skin layer called the stratum lucidum found?
explanation: The stratum lucidum is a clear, protective layer found only in areas of thick skin that deal with a lot of friction, like the palms of the hands and soles of the feet. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h3)

question: What is the main feature of cells in the deepest layer of the epidermis (stratum basale)?
explanation: The stratum basale contains cells that constantly divide to create new cells that push upward toward the skin surface. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h3)

question: What type of tissue makes up the reticular layer of the dermis?
explanation: The reticular layer is packed with thick collagen fibers running in different directions to give the skin strength and toughness. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h4)

question: Dermal papillae help form which unique feature on the hands and feet?
explanation: Bumps from the upper dermal layer push up against the epidermis, creating the unique ridges we know as fingerprints and footprints. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h4)

question: What is the main type of tissue found in the hypodermis (subcutaneous layer)?
explanation: The hypodermis is mostly made of fat tissue (adipose tissue), which helps insulate the body, provide padding, and store energy. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is the job of oil (sebaceous) glands in the skin?

options.A: Anchoring epidermal layers to underlying muscle
options.B: Lubricating and waterproofing skin and hair
options.C: Providing immune defense against bacterial invasion
options.D: Regulating core body temperature via evaporation

explanation: Sebaceous glands produce oil (sebum) that keeps the skin soft and stops it from losing too much water. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h5)

question: A patient gets a pressure sore over the tailbone from lying in bed too long. What happens first to cause this tissue breakdown?

options.A: Hypersecretion of sebum blocking epidermal pores
options.B: Atrophy of melanocytes leading to radiation damage
options.C: Compression of blood vessels in the dermis and hypodermis
options.D: Accelerated mitotic division in the stratum basale

explanation: Constant pressure squeezes blood vessels shut, cutting off oxygen and nutrients to the skin layers and causing cells to die. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h6)

question: Why do nurses check skin turgor over the collarbone (clavicle) or chest instead of the back of the hand in older adults?

options.A: The clavicle has higher concentration of sweat glands for fluid testing
options.B: Loss of subcutaneous fat in the hands creates false dehydration readings
options.C: Skin on the hand lacks the collagen fibers necessary for elasticity
options.D: Blood flow to the extremities prevents accurate moisture measurement

explanation: Older adults lose fat and skin elasticity in their hands, so checking the chest or collarbone gives a much truer picture of hydration. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h6)
